page.overview:
Who is Echidna?

Echidna is part of Greek mythology. Echidna is a monster in Greek mythology, depicted as half-woman and half-snake, known as the "Mother of Monsters." She was the mate of Typhon and the mother of many famous mythical creatures, including the Hydra and Cerberus, representing chaos and danger in ancient stories.

While there is no direct reference to Echidna in the Cthulhu Mythos created by H. P. Lovecraft and later authors, several parallels can be drawn.

In Chaosium's roleplaying game Call of Cthulhu, while Echidna herself does not appear directly, her relatives—such as her mother Ceto, her mate Typhon, and her offspring Cerberus—do make appearances. (: Cthulhu Invictus)

Echidna is the granddaughter of the Elder God Set born to his son Phorcys who mated with Ceto, a sea monster. She has sired many of the monsters of Greek mythology, most of which the heroic demi-god Hercules has battled. Most of them were sired with Typhon, one of the Titans, except for Angerboda who she sired with Varcolac and the Snakes of Many Colors.
